scores.round_files_fidelity_rationale: All three files are close transliterations. ubx_m8p: the framing state machine matches case by case. That includes the default/case-0 merge, the 'payloadlen > buffer.Length' reset after step++, the zero-length payload stall, the overrun at msglencount+6 that throws before msglencount++, and the checksum over [2, payloadlen+6). Every struct size checks out against Pack=1 (mon_ver 70, mon_hw 60, nav_pvt 92, nav_svin 40, nav_velned 36, cfg_nav5 36, cfg_tmode3 40). The tmode3 constructors keep the ECEF/LLA split on |lat| > 90, the (int)/(sbyte)/(uint) casts through the shim and the HP arithmetic order. to_bytes pads or truncates reserved3 to 8 bytes as StructureToByteArray's Array.Resize does. getPointLatLngAlt keeps the C# quirk of returning ECEF metres in Lat/Lng/Alt. SetupM8P, SetupBasePos, turnon_off and poll_msg send the same bytes in the same order with the same sleeps. Spline2 keeps the float/double mix (1.0e7f, 0.1f and LATLON_TO_CM widened, 1.0e-7f float products, float lengths, (float)Math.Sqrt of a float product), stores the static speeds as f32 bits, models the null _origin/_destination/_hermite_spline_solution, and wraps update_spline's uint subtraction. RLE keeps the dropped last byte and the 250 split. Its Huffman tree uses a stable sort (OrderBy), sets Root only inside the loop and keeps Dictionary insertion order; Delta wraps. Points are lost for: the UBX structs bypassing MavlinkUtil/MarshalStruct, with short-buffer semantics that differ from ByteArrayToStructure and are documented wrongly; panics where C# throws on a replaced public buffer; Spline2's up-front null check, which skips C#'s partial side effects; Encode/Decode rejecting a null Root even when C# never dereferences it; HuffMan.test writing compact JSON where ToJSON() is Formatting.Indented; JSON error paths and byte? coercion; the class/reference semantics collapsed again; the inherited Utils member dropped; and self-consistency tests with tolerances instead of C# golden data.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Mavlink/MavlinkUtil.cs:15 (UseUnsafe = true), 25-32 (ByteArrayToStructure<T>(bytearray, startoffset = 6)), 119-130 (ReadUsingPointer returns default(T) when data.Length - startoffset < SizeOf(T)), 270-307 (StructureToByteArray, generic over any struct); ubx_m8p.cs:382-385; crates/mp-core/src/extlibs/mavlink/mavlinkutil.rs:13-22 (MarshalStruct)
findings.summary: The six UBX structs ignore the existing MavlinkUtil port. In C# they are read with packet.ByteArrayToStructure<Ubx.ubx_nav_svin>(6) and written with MavlinkUtil.StructureToByteArray. The Rust structs do not implement MarshalStruct, so MavlinkUtil::byte_array_to_structure / structure_to_byte_array_t / the big-endian variants cannot take them, and there is no FieldInfo table. The header comment (:5-7) says from_bytes matches ByteArrayToStructure with 'a short buffer leaves the remaining fields zero'. That is wrong: with UseUnsafe (the default), a buffer shorter than startoffset + SizeOf(T) returns default(T), with every field zero and every byte[] null, not a partially decoded struct. from_bytes also has no startoffset parameter (C# default 6). Only ubx_cfg_tmode3 has to_bytes, while C# StructureToByteArray serialises any of them.
findings.required_fix: Implement MarshalStruct (SIZE, fields(), from_bytes, to_bytes) for ubx_mon_ver, ubx_mon_hw, ubx_nav_pvt, ubx_nav_svin, ubx_nav_velned, ubx_cfg_nav5_getset_s and ubx_cfg_tmode3. Route the tmode3 byte[] conversion through MavlinkUtil::structure_to_byte_array_t, and let callers decode through MavlinkUtil::byte_array_to_structure(buf, 6). Fix the doc comment. Add a test that a short buffer yields the default struct.

findings.cs_reference: ubx_m8p.cs:18 (public byte[] buffer), 22-30 (@class/subclass getters), 53-95 (Read steps 0-5 index buffer[0..5]), 574-616 (SetupBasePos dereferences basepos)
findings.summary: Panics where C# throws, and nullability is lost. 'buffer' is a public field in both versions, and a caller can replace it with a shorter array. class() (:493), subclass() (:498) and Read steps 0-5 (:509, :516, :520, :524, :529, :570) index self.buffer directly and panic, where C# throws IndexOutOfRangeException out of Read (or NullReferenceException for null). Steps 6-8 already go through put(). SetupBasePos takes &PointLatLngAlt. In C# a null basepos passes 'basepos == PointLatLngAlt.Zero' (false, through the null-aware operator) and then throws NullReferenceException at basepos.Lat, after the two 100 ms sleeps. That path cannot be expressed.
findings.required_fix: Use buffer.get(i).ok_or_else(index_out_of_range) (and get_mut) in every step and in class()/subclass(), returning Result. Take basepos as Option<&PointLatLngAlt>: None compares unequal to Zero and then fails with NullReference at the fixed-position branch, in C# order.

findings.cs_reference: Spline2.cs:139-162 (origin = _destination or _origin, possibly null), 180-244 (first dereference of origin depends on the branch)
findings.summary: set_spline_destination rejects a null origin before calling set_spline_origin_and_destination. C# hits the NullReferenceException at the first arithmetic use, and on some paths it mutates state first. Take reached_destination = true (the public _flags allows it with _destination null), stopped_at_start = false and segment_type = SEGMENT_SPLINE. C# then assigns _spline_origin_vel = _spline_destination_vel, rewrites _spline_time (minus 1, or 0) and zeroes _spline_vel_scaler. With SEGMENT_END_STRAIGHT it also assigns _spline_destination_vel and sets fast_waypoint = true, and only then throws at '(destination - origin).length()'. Rust throws with none of those writes. A caller that catches the exception sees different object state.
findings.required_fix: Remove the pre-check. Pass Option<Vector3> origin into set_spline_origin_and_destination and unwrap it with NullReference at each C# use site, in C# evaluation order: the stopped branch's (destination - origin), the STOP/SPLINE end-type arms and pos_len.

findings.cs_reference: RLE.cs:206-228 (Root dereferenced inside the loop; returns BitArray), 230-263 (current = Root; dereferenced on the first bit)
findings.summary: Encode and Decode check Root up front. In C#, Encode with an empty source never touches this.Root and returns an empty BitArray, and Decode with an empty BitArray returns an empty byte[], both even when Root is null (for example after BuildHuffmanTree on a single-symbol input). Rust returns NullReferenceException in both cases. The C# BitArray return/parameter type is also replaced by Vec<bool>, so BitArray members such as Length, Get/Set and CopyTo are missing.
findings.required_fix: Dereference Root lazily: inside the per-byte loop in Encode and on the first bit in Decode. Add a small dotnet BitArray (or document the Vec<bool> mapping) and test the empty/null-root cases.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/Extensions.cs:413-430 (ToJSON(object) => SerializeObject(msg, Formatting.Indented, Error handler sets Handled)); RLE.cs:127-131; Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3 (MissionPlanner.Utilities.csproj:52) DefaultMaxDepth = 64, JsonSerializerInternalReader.EnsureType for byte?
findings.summary: (1) HuffMan.test writes huff.json with to_compact. In C#, huff.Root.ToJSON() is Formatting.Indented: two-space indent and Environment.NewLine, so the file bytes differ. (2) The Symbol error at from_v :134 formats "Path '{path}.Symbol'", which gives "Path '.Symbol'" for the root object. Newtonsoft writes "Path 'Symbol', line 1, position N." (the child path from JsonObj::get, plus line/position). (3) Symbol is read with read_int's Int32 rules, but byte? goes through ReadType.Read and Convert.ChangeType. A token of 5.0 or "5" converts in C#, while Rust rejects 5.0 ('Input string ... not a valid integer'). 3000000000 gives "Error converting value 3000000000 to type 'System.Nullable`1[System.Byte]'" in C#, not the Int32 overflow text. (4) Newtonsoft 13 stops at MaxDepth 64 with a JsonReaderException. The Rust recursion has no such limit below serde_json's 128, so trees 64-127 levels deep deserialise in Rust and fail in C#.
findings.required_fix: Use to_j().to_indented() in to_json (ToJSON's default). Build the Symbol error from the path returned by o.get("Symbol") and add the line/position suffix. Read byte? with Newtonsoft's ChangeType rules (integral doubles and numeric strings accepted, 'Error converting value' for overflow). Enforce MaxDepth 64 in from_v with Newtonsoft's message.

findings.cs_reference: Spline2.cs:8 (class), 59-60/126-127/264-265 (_origin/_destination alias the caller's Vector3 objects), 339 (ref target_pos); Vector3.cs:19/34 (class Vector3<T>); RLE.cs:62/153/181-202 (class Node, List.Remove by reference, Root = nodes.FirstOrDefault()); ubx_m8p.cs:14 (class Ubx), 170-411 (structs whose byte[] fields are shared on copy)
findings.summary: R59-14 continues into this batch. Spline2, Ubx, Node and HuffmanTree are classes but derive Clone, and Node derives value PartialEq where C# has reference identity. Spline2 stores copies where C# keeps references to the caller's Vector3 objects, so a later 'origin.x = ...' by the caller changes C#'s _origin and not Rust's. In the spline-segment branch, _spline_origin_vel and _spline_destination_vel alias each other until the next reassignment. HuffmanTree.Root is a deep clone of nodes[0], while in C# Root is that node, so writes through Root reach nodes and later BuildHuffmanTree calls. Copying a UBX struct in C# shares its byte[] fields; Rust clones the Vecs.
findings.required_fix: Drop the Clone/PartialEq derives the C# types do not have. Hold Node as Rc<RefCell<Node>> (or arena indices) so Root and nodes share identity, and hold Spline2's Vector3 fields as shared handles, or document every call site that relies on value semantics.

Re-export the nested types under modules named after their owners (huff_man::Node, ubx_cfg_tmode3_types::modeflags). Use Option<Vec<u8>> for the ByValArray fields.

verdict: This round adds 3 file-mirrored ports (1,348 C# lines): ubx_m8p (Ubx), Spline2 and RLE (RLE/HuffMan/Delta). It also fixes the crc24q panic and adds CR LF, broken-pipe-safe Console helpers. The ports are faithful at the level of bytes and floats: the UBX state machine, checksum, struct sizes, tmode3 casts and setup transcripts match, Spline2 keeps the float/double mix and the uint wrap, and the Huffman build keeps stable-sort ties and the Root-only-in-loop quirk. No definite compile error was found. What remains: the UBX structs bypass MavlinkUtil, and their short-buffer semantics are documented wrongly; there are panics and eager null checks where C# throws later; HuffMan.test writes compact JSON instead of indented; JSON errors and byte? coercion differ; class semantics are collapsed again; Spline2's inherited Utils member is missing; the tests are self-consistency only; and println! remains in five ported files. Nothing is wired. The app still runs rtk.rs, which now duplicates and diverges from ubx_m8p, and it draws spline waypoints straight. Owned progress is about 5.3% (25,516 / 479,014), so the cap is 1.6. Awarded 1.0; round-file fidelity is 6.9/10.
